hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y (positive gain).
Response has lag/delay of tens of seconds, not instantaneous.
No large dead-zone: u=0.5 produces rise clearly above noise.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward low ambient.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear across u levels.
Steady-state u needed to hold y=0.5 is in mid-range [0.3,0.7].
Sensor noise is small (<0.01) so trends are interpretable.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Primary gain direction/magnitude and response lag, which determine all subsequent safe steps and controller sizing.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive-gain heater hypothesis is right, y will rise from ~0.08 toward 0.3-0.5 over 180s with visible lag of tens of seconds and positive end-slope indicating not yet settled.
proposal.readiness_justification: No experiments completed yet, so gain, lag, dead-zone, decay, linearity, hold-input and noise uncertainties are all unresolved; at least three experiments are required before a controller can be justified.
proposal.operator_note: First probe with mid-power 0.5 for full 180s to measure direction, size and lag of heating response.

proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound with no decay or lag: 0.4429 + 0.006*0.5*120 = 0.8029, which stays below soft limit 0.85 with margin, and well below hard cutoff 0.9.
proposal.expected_observation: If large-lag positive-gain hypothesis is right, y will continue rising from ~0.44 toward ~0.53-0.58 over 120s with gradually declining but still positive end-slope (~0.0008-0.0012), staying well below soft limit and proving equilibrium for u=0.5 is above 0.5.
proposal.readiness_justification: Only E1 completed so minimum-3 rule not met. Resolved: direction is positive, no dead-zone at 0.5, noise small. Unresolved: exact steady-state gain and time constant (E1 slope still 0.0014/s, not settled), decay rate at u=0, linearity across levels, and exact hold-input for 0.5. Not yet safe to generate controller.
proposal.operator_note: Heater shows strong upward response at half power; holding half power 2 more minutes to measure settling before testing lower powers.

proposal.operator_note: Holding at u=0.5 reached ~0.54 above target; now stepping to zero for 180s to measure cooldown rate.

proposal.expected_observation: If linear first-order hypothesis with tau~110-150s and y_ss(0.45)~0.49-0.50 is right, y will rise from ~0.448 toward ~0.48-0.495 over 140s with declining but still slightly positive end-slope ~0.0003-0.0007, entering the lower edge of the 0.475-0.525 band and staying far below limits.
proposal.readiness_justification: Direction, lag order, self-cooling, small noise, and approximate hold-input bracket are resolved, but E4 ended with slope 0.0012 so equilibrium for u=0.45 is not yet measured and linearity rests on only two settled/projected points, so one more settling hold is needed before a controller can be sized with confidence.
proposal.operator_note: Continuing 0.45 hold to observe settling toward target band and confirm hold power.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y (positive gain).
Response has lag/time-constant of order 120-160s, settling takes ~300-400s, not instantaneous.
No large dead-zone: u=0.45 and u=0.5 produce rise clearly above noise.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward low ambient near 0.08.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear across u levels on original plant.
Steady-state u needed to hold y=0.5 was near 0.39-0.44 on original plant; after change higher u is needed.
Sensor noise is small (<0.01) so trends are interpretable, quantization ~0.005.
Change is weaker actuator: same u holds lower y, but u=0 cooling rate, delay and ambient asymptote are unchanged.
Change is faster outflow/heat loss: u=0 cools faster and same u holds lower y.
Change is slower response: distinctly longer pure delay or larger time constant with similar steady-state gain.
Change is sensor offset or noise change: true thermal response unchanged but readings shifted or noisier.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Measures unforced cooling rate, pure delay, and ambient asymptote at u=0 to discriminate weaker gain (same cooling) from faster outflow (faster cooling), slower response (longer delay), and sensor offset (shifted asymptote), which determines feedforward and tuning for redesign.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound is 0.4591 + 0.006*0*300 = 0.4591, well below 0.85 soft limit and 0.9 hard cutoff; u=0 can only cool from a moderate level.
proposal.expected_observation: If leading weaker-gain hypothesis is right, y will hold near 0.459 for ~10-15s for delay then fall monotonically toward ambient, reaching ~0.10-0.18 after 300s on a trajectory similar to E3; faster fall implies faster outflow, longer flat implies slower response, shifted asymptote or larger scatter implies sensor change.
proposal.readiness_justification: Original gain, lag and ambient are well characterized, and monitoring shows higher u is now needed for 0.5, but gain loss vs faster loss vs slower response vs sensor offset are not yet isolated with a controlled after-change experiment, so not ready to generate.
proposal.operator_note: Draining at zero power to measure cooling speed, delay and ambient on the changed plant.
